content:
sam: quick Q — where's the best place to pull a per-tenant SLO breakdown for last night's spike (~2026-03-15 02:15–02:40 UTC)? need uptime + 95p latency slices and traces for suspected throttling. also: burn-rate alert fired for the window; can we exclude canary/internal test traffic from that monitor? cc @miriam @rajesh

miriam: Dashboards: https://dash.redwood.io/d/ops/slo-overview (use the tenant dropdown) and traces: https://traces.redwood.io/search -> filter by time + request.customer_id. For the burn-rate monitor (DD monitor #1234) we currently don't filter env tags, so canary noise will trigger it. Recommend adding `!env:canary` to the monitor query and also tagging canary requests with `internal=true` consistently.

rajesh: +1 on excluding canary. If we change monitor #1234 I'll also add a temporary annotation/maintenance window for the deploys this week so historical alerts don't skew burn-rate. Do we want an explicit list of customer_ids to ignore or just the env tag?

sam: env tag is easiest (we already have `env:canary` on the perf tests). prefer tag over explicit id list. also need the exact PromQL/log queries so I can pull CSV for the PM.

miriam: PromQL (SLO error rate slice): `sum(rate(requests_total{job="api",status!~"2..",env!="canary"}[5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total{job="api",env!="canary"}[5m]))` — tweak labels as needed. 

miriam: Logs (Datadog): `@service:api AND @env:!canary AND @customer_id:{*} AND @status:error` — use the time range and split by `@customer_id` to get per-tenant counts.

oliver: Loki snippet if anyone needs it: ```{app="api", env!="canary"} |= "500" | json | line_format "{customer_id} {latency_ms}"``` then aggregate by `customer_id` and `histogram_quantile(0.95, ...)`.

reliability-bot: Monitor #1234 triggered 2026-03-15T02:22:18Z — burn rate 4.6x for service:api (alert_id=mk-1234).

rajesh: I'll open a quick PR to update the Datadog monitor to add env exclusion and add an option to ignore `internal=true` as well. Ping me here if you want me to also add a short runbook note about canary tagging.

sam: please do. also can someone add an SLO annotation at 02:15–02:40 for the incident? want it visible on the SLO dash when I export.

miriam: done — added annotation on SLO dash and created runbook note: https://wiki.redwood.io/sre/incidents/slo-canary-filtering. PR #452 will be the monitor change, assigning to @rajesh.

sam: perfect, thanks :thumbsup:
